summary: Umar completed his B.A. with Honors in the English Language and Literature in 2000 and M.A. in English Linguistics at the University of Baghdad in 2004. He taught in different educational settings in Baghdad/Iraq from private language institutes to public and private universities. In 2006, he received one of the Fulbright scholarships to complete his M.A. in TESOL at the Indiana University of Pennsylvania. In 2009, he joined Ohio Northern University to teach ESL/ESP and the following year, he was appointed the director of ESP for the Prison Management Certificate Program. At Ohio Northern University, Umar developed the Arabic language program at the department of modern languages. Currently, Umar is teaching ESL for Global Launch/Arizona State University. Additionally, Umar is pursuing his PhD in Linguistics and Applied Linguistics at ASU.

middle_initial: My research concentrated on the study of brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs) and their interactions with circulating breast tumor cells (CBTCs), following their extravasation to the brain. We hope to continue to address the mechanism(s) by which CBTCs are able to breach and infiltrate the BBB to form metastases in brain. We will examine the kinetics and the changes in tight junctions expression and localization in BMECs, the activation of BMECs by CBTCs and their interactions with each other, leading to co-option, colonization and metastasis formation in brain, using in vivo mice models. We will specifically focus on the unique Angiopoietin-2/Tie-2 pathway in the BBB and BMECs that is activated by CBTCs. This investigation may help in the clinical setting, to prevent brain metastasis at an early stage of this disease by inhibiting Ang-2/Tie-2 axis alone or in combination with already clinically used drugs, such as Enbrel that targets TNF-alpha.
